title: Assurance scratch: control lifecycle sketch - Juno
content:
Quick sketch of control lifecycle ideas, evidence flows, and open questions for SOC2 prep. Meant to be a messy brain dump before I turn this into a more formal mapping doc.

Context / goal:
- We need a minimal, testable set of controls that cover logical access, change management, deployment, and monitoring for Redwood Private + Dedicated.
- Ensure evidence collection is automatable where possible (logs, config exports) and map manual attestations where automation isn't feasible.

High-level control buckets (working):
- Identity & Access Management (IAM/SAML/Okta)
- Key lifecycle (KMS/HSM usage, rotation, access audit)
- Network isolation (VPC peering, private endpoints, firewall rules)
- Deployment / Change Control (PR gating, CI checks, canary rollouts)
- Runtime protections (secrets handling, process isolation)
- Observability & incident response (tracing, alerting, postmortems)
- Data handling & retention (customer data flows, deletion requests)

Mapping notes (rough pairs: control -> evidence -> owner -> automation level):
- IAM: control=unique accounts + MFA + role review every 90d; evidence=Okta export (users.csv), last 90d sign-in logs, MFA enforcement policy; owner=security-ops; automation=high (scripted exports + CI job).
- KMS: control=CMKs for customer keys + rotation policy; evidence=KMS key metadata, rotation timestamps, IAM policy statements; owner=infra-crypto; automation=medium (AWS exports + manual verification for HSM-backed keys).
- VPC: control=private deployments must be in isolated VPCs with no public subnets; evidence=Terraform plan outputs, route table configs, security group rules; owner=platform-eng; automation=high (terraform state snapshot).
- Deploy/change control: control=every change to runtime must go through pipeline with automated tests + approval for prod; evidence=GitHub PR links, CI run artifacts, deployment timestamps; owner=release-eng; automation=high.

Practical evidence checklist (initial):
- Okta: users CSV + group membership export (admin console)
- GitHub: PR link + merge commit + pipeline logs (artifact links)
- Terraform: state snapshot + plan outputs for last deploy (store in S3 versioned)
- KMS: list-keys + key-rotation-status command output + who-allowed-policy JSON
- Console screenshots only if automation impossible (mark as manual evidence, include exact query/filters used)

Sample control test (draft):
- Control: Prod API tokens are rotated every 90 days and stored in KMS-wrapped secrets.
- Test procedure: Query secrets-store for token creation dates (aws secretsmanager list-secret-versions), filter tokens older than 90d. Cross-check with KMS key rotation logs. Pull one PR that rotated token (if manual) and attach PR link.
- Expected evidence: CSV of tokens with creation_date; KMS key rotation history; PR link or Ops ticket.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- How do we handle customer-managed keys vs platform-managed keys in the evidence model? (one control or two?)
- Acceptable proof for network isolation: terraform state vs runtime verification (nmap?) — auditors often prefer config artifacts. Keep both.
- API keys stored in vault: do we snapshot hashes or full metadata? Avoid storing plaintext. Need canonical query for secrets age.
- Which logs are retained centrally and for how long (alerts team asked for 30d, SOC2 might require 90d+ depending on criteria).

Notes to self (todo):
- [ ] Draft a control matrix CSV: columns = control_id, title, owner, description, evidence_queries, evidence_location, automation_level, test_steps, linked_jira.
- [ ] Build Terraform state snapshot pipeline (S3 version + tag) and document snapshot retrieval steps.
- [ ] Write small scripts to export Okta users and last-auth times to a standard S3 path.
- [ ] Coordinate with infra-crypto on HSM evidence (who can sign off manual checks).
- [ ] Liaise with support to capture ticket samples for data deletion requests (anonymize customer ids).

Quick troubleshooting heuristics (for auditors):
- If an exported artifact is incomplete, provide the exact CLI command used + timestamp + request ID for reproducibility.
- If a policy file is large, provide a trimmed diff that highlights the policy lines relevant to the control, plus a link to the full blob.

Conversation snippets to follow up (Slack refs):
- #trust-ops: thread about KMS HSM backup (ask Marci for list of HSM-backed keys).
- #platform-deploys: note about canary rollback metric thresholds (need capture).

Minimal examples of queries / commands to capture evidence (save these in repo under /tools/evidence-scripts):
- Okta users export: curl -H "Authorization: SSWS $OKTA_TOKEN" "https://redwood.okta.com/api/v1/users?limit=200" > okta-users-$(date +%F).json
- List KMS keys: aws kms list-keys --profile prod --region us-west-2 --query 'Keys[].KeyId' > kms-keys-$(date +%F).txt
- Terraform plan output: terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan && terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan-$(date +%F).json

Risks / red flags we should watch for during evidence collection:
- Too many manual screenshots: increases audit friction. Prioritize CLI/JSON exports.
- Discrepancies between terraform state and actual cloud state (drift) — note drift run in evidence.
- Stale service accounts with broad permissions — create a short script to grep for last-used timestamps.

Suggested next steps for a polished mapping doc (owner assigned):
- Create control matrix CSV (Juno) — due 2026-03-08
- Instrument automated exports: Okta + KMS + Terraform (Marcus) — due 2026-03-15
- Draft test procedures & sample evidence templates (Ava) — due 2026-03-12
- Run a dry collection run and document gaps (team run 2026-03-20)

Random brainstorm ideas (probably not for v1, but keep):
- Evidence registry: small service that stores references to artifacts with metadata (type, query used, freshness, sha256) so auditors can fetch canonical items. Minimal UI to search by control_id.
- Control maturity score: quick 1-5 based on automation + evidence freshness + owner SLA. Useful for roadmap prioritization.

End messy dump. Will clean up into a spreadsheet and a Confluence page next.

-- Juno
